newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel clears plan to sell Bezeq stake.
newsitem.headline: Israel clears plan to sell Bezeq stake.

text.p: Israel's ministerial privatisation committee on Thursday approved a plan to sell 25 percent of Bezeq Israel Telecom, reducing its holding to 51 percent by the end of the year, an official said.

Moshe Leon, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's chief economics adviser, said the plan called for selling part of the shares -- probably 10 percent -- through a public offering in the Israeli capital market. The rest would be sold by other means yet to be determined, he said.
Leon told Reuters that the domestic public flotation would be in another two to three months. He refused to speculate on how the remaining shares would be sold.

The government holds 76 percent of Bezeq, Israel's main telecommunications carrier. The rest trades on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, although about half the float is controlled by Britain's Cable and Wireless PLC.
Israel has been in lengthy negotiations with Cable and Wireless over the British company's future role in Bezeq, but officials said no agreement had yet been reached.

Communications Minister Limor Livnat and other officials have been pushing hard to speed the privatisation of Bezeq. Shares in the company were supposed to be floated in a global offering, but in February she approved a plan for a domestic offering on the grounds it could be done more quickly.

Government sources said they hoped they could raise about $500 million from the sale of the 25 percent stake. Bezeq's market capitalisation is currently $1.9 billion. Part of the proceeds might go to the company itself, they added.

Bezeq officials have said they would prefer a global offering, which would raise the company's profile in international financial markets. In addition, the weakness of the Tel Aviv stock exchange precludes floating all the shares domestically, officials have said.
